contexts.text: Ships () = Knowledges of truth which are corrupt.
Would believe that the ships would fall off.
Ships of Tarshish () = Knowledges. ( = doctrinals and truths from the Word. AC 6385.) ( = doctrinals of truth and good. AC 9295:7.)
I dreamed that a ship came with all kinds of delicious things to eat. Described. SE 3380.
At the haven of ships () = where are doctrinal things from the Word.
The reason ships = doctrinal things from the Word, is that they pass through seas and rivers, and carry things useful for life. Explained, Illustrated.
These Knowledges are described by such things as belong to a ship. Enumerated. AE 514:2.
As ships = Knowledges and doctrinals, it is said, they that go down to the sea with ships, these have seen the works of Jehovah... ().

The third part of the ships was broken () = that the truths and goods of doctrinals... were falsified. ( = that all the Knowledges of good and truth from the Word, of service for the use of life, had been destroyed with them. AR 406. AE 514.)
Ships, in the opposite, = Knowledges and doctrinals of what is false and evil. Illustrated.
Ships = doctrinal things from the Word.
Ships appear in the other life... and those in the ships there = those who vend and instruct in such things.
The ships () = Knowledges and doctrinal things from the Word.
As a hidden current carries a ship. DP 198:end. AE 457.
Ships = Knowledges of good and truth. Illustrated.
A magnificent dock in which were vessels great and small, seen. Explained. TCR 462.
A vessel with seven sails seen flying in the air. Described, Explained, TCR 462:6.
Ships = spiritual merchandize, which is the Knowledges of truth and good; here () natural merchandize... AR 789.
Lest the tempest... submerge the ship...
Like those who weave a little ship of reeds.
Like a ship laden with wares of greatest value, storm driven...
Like a little ship which can sail with the wind or against it.
Carried away like ships... while hypocrites steer.
(A dream of crossing a tumultuous sea in a vessel.)
(A dream of a ship.)
They then represent a ship.
Ships of Tarshish = general Knowledges of truth and good in which are many things in particular. AE 304:27. Compare AE 406:10. AE 410:3. AE 514:5, AE 514:6, AE 514:7, AE 514:8, AE 514:9.
Ships = scientific and doctrinal things in both senses. Illustrated.
Ships = Knowledges of truth and good from the Word.
Ships = doctrinal things and Knowledges of all kinds.
To cast the net on the right side of the ship () = that all things [be done] from the good of love and of charity. AE 600:7.

Ships = Knowledges of good and truth, also doctrinals, because they carry wealth over the sea for trading... In a restricted sense, in which the containant is meant, ships = the Word, and doctrine from it, because these contain Knowledges of truth and good, as ships contain wealth; and to trade, which is especially done by means of ships, = to procure Knowledges and communicate them to others. But when the contents are understood, ships = Knowledges from the Word, and from doctrine from the Word. Illustrated.

A ship of oar () = intelligence from proprium, because propelled by men; a magnificent ship = wisdom from proprium... For a ship = intelligence and wisdom when it goes to sea and passes across; for so it is in its course, carrying wealth.
They that go down to the sea in ships, doing work in many waters = those who intently study the doctrine of truth from the Word.
Ships = falsities and falsifications of truth of every kind.
Ships from the coast of Chittim () = Knowledges of truth and good possessed by the Ancient Church.
Why shall Dan fear ships? () = why did he not repel falsities and doctrinals of falsity?
The Lord taught from a ship because a ship = to teach from doctrine. Illustrated.
The ships of Tyre = the Knowledges of good and truth, or the truths of the natural man, which they acquire and which they vend; here, Falsities. AE 1146:2.
Those employed upon ships () = those in intelligence.
To have ships in the sea () = to confirm these things by reasonings from the natural man.
Like water with a wrecked ship below.
Like a wrecked ship of which only the top of the mast protrudes.
